page: Microsoft Azure F64als_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine hosted on Microsoft Hyper-V, utilizing the AMD EPYC 9V45 processor. It provides 64 dedicated physical x86_64 cores operating at up to 4.5 GHz, configured with 1 thread per core. The cache structure comprises 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Supported instruction set extensions include AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AVX-512 BF16, and cryptographic accelerators like VAES and AES. The instance is provisioned with 128.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a lean 2.0 GB per core ratio.

The F64als_v7 does not bundle local disk storage or GPU accelerators, relying on remote block storage solutions such as Azure Premium Storage for persistent workloads. Benchmark results show top-tier multi-core compute capability, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 233,270.61 and a PassMark CPU score of 116,710.13. The memory subsystem demonstrated 410.03 GB/sec in large uncached read operations and 205.23 GB/sec in large write operations. The instance also registered high data processing rates, including 869.45 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, 171.03 million Redis SET operations per second, and 103.82 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

By omitting local disks and maintaining a low RAM-to-CPU ratio, the F64als_v7 delivers high compute density without the overhead of unneeded memory capacity. The primary tradeoff is the requirement for external storage and lower per-core RAM headroom. This hardware configuration fits parallel, compute-intensive workloads including software compilation, batch compression, mathematical modeling, high-throughput web frontends, and small-to-medium scale LLM CPU inference.
description: Microsoft Azure F64als_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine equipped with 64 dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 physical cores running at up to 4.5 GHz on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides 128.0 GB of RAM, offering a lean 2.0 GB per vCPU allocation tailored for compute-heavy tasks rather than memory-heavy datasets. Vector execution is enhanced by AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16 instructions. The instance does not include local disk storage or hardware GPUs, depending entirely on external Azure Premium Storage for persistence. In standardized benchmarks, F64als_v7 recorded top-tier multi-core stress-ng performance of 233,270.61, PassMark CPU scores of 116,710.13, and uncached memory read bandwidth of 410.03 GB/sec. It also achieved 171.03 million Redis operations per second and 103.82 GB/sec static web throughput. This server offers cost-efficient compute density for workloads such as batch processing, multi-threaded compression, simulation, and high-volume web serving where high memory overhead is unnecessary.
